Messages.Author: librarian
Messages.Body:
I hope I am proven wrong, but I think the Montreal NAC will have similar
numbers to the Los Angeles NAC last year, i.e. pretty low.

It seems to me that the highest number of NAC were either at the Atlanta
one held near WW's headquarters, or at GenCon the year before.

The rotating idea works in Europe, but for the US, I think a steady
location will work better. Finding a venue is easier when you can lock
in a specific weekend each year. Folks can make travel plans earlier,
and perhaps get better deals.

It does however put a particular onus on the local volunteers (in the
case of Atlanta - Lasombra, Tatus, and others); but by the same token,
perhaps WW staff could take up more of the load. Or perhaps out-of-town
princes could be the "hosts" of the event, and as a reward get a card
specifically for their town, or something. As hosts, they would judge
events, including Week of Nightmare events, and perhaps come up with the
events schedule for WoN as well. And then as a reward, they would get a
shweet card, like Powerbase Columbus; Crusade Berkeley; Fee Stake Boston
(oh, too late), etc.

Thoughts? Am I crazy, do I not see things correctly?

best -

chris

Messages.Author: ira...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:


It seems to me that the biggest factor in determining attendance at
the NAC is cost to attend. The higher the cost, the lower the
attendance. I think a secondary factor is how many qualified players
there are. It would be interesting to know how many qualified players
there are this year, last year, and the year before. Robyn/Oscar, do
you have that data, and if so, can you share it?

I think an unchanging weekend, or a fixed city, isn't a key factor in
determining attendance, assuming the location and date are announced
enough in advance. I'd aim for 1 year in advance. I also think that
organizing the event each year would be too much burden for a single
group of people, and it would also be unfair to players who are far
away from that city.

The cost to attend the Montreal NAC is a lot higher for me (since I
live in San Francisco), but perhaps a lot lower for more people (who
live in Montreal, or the Northeast.)

Ira

Messages.Author: ben...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Ira wrote:
> It seems to me that the biggest factor in determining attendance at
> the NAC is cost to attend.

I'm very certain this is true. A big factor with respect to that is
the demographics of the North American players. We're basically
loaded onto the eastern half of North America. Most players had to
cross plains, mountains, and desert in order to get to the NAC in LA.
Lowering the travel cost would be a big step towards increasing
attendance. It may be the case that keeping the NAC in the middle (or
slightly east of middle) of North America is the right approach for
maintaining a high attendance. However, there's also the sentiment
that by moving the NAC around, it gives every region a chance to
attend - it's one of the big reasons why we went with that system.
I've also had some players tell me that they have to make the choice
between attending GenCon and attending the NAC, and they've been
choosing GenCon.

I'm certainly open to suggestions as to where we think the NAC
should be in future years. We could keep moving from city to city.
We could go back to GenCon. Do we tell Seattle to just suck it up and
deal while we try to maximize attendance, or do we try to put the NAC
in the Pacific Northwest sometime? Do we have it in Mexico City?

Here's another factor: I haven't really gotten many people
volunteering to host the 2009 NAC. Ira's offered to have it in San
Francisco. Kevin's mulled over having it in Las Vegas. I've thought
about having it in Boston. I'm not sure if it's true in Ira's case,
but Kevin and I are really concerned about the cost of the event. I'm
rather pessimistic about how much it would cost to have the NAC
weekend plus the Week of Nightmares in the Boston area. Speaking of
which, as fun and as great a tradition as the Week of Nightmares is,
it's definitely a burden on the organizers to accomodate it - it might
be a reason why I've gotten few volunteers. I certainly don't expect
to have free run of The Ram at GenCon if we were to move back.

Thoughts? Ideas? Comments? Volunteers? :)

- Ben Peal, US National Coordinator

To be clear, I inquired about the process to submit a bid to host the
NAC in San Francisco. :) I now understand what is required to submit
a bid, but I don't know the deadline for that submission. For the
most significant VTES event in all of North America, it seems
reasonable to me to set a deadline for when bids must be submitted.

Ben or Oscar, can you tell me (and everyone) what is the deadline to
submit a bid to host the NAC 2009?

If a group isn't well enough organized to submit a bid by the
deadline, then they probably aren't well-organized enough to run the
event. Also, by having a publicized deadline, it makes it a more fair
submission process.

> I'm not sure if it's true in Ira's case, but Kevin and I
> are really concerned about the cost of the event.

I think Kevin is less concerned now that he's found a good place. I'm
not certain that he's actually considering submitting a bid, though.

For San Francisco area, I'm definitely concerned about the cost of the
event, but I haven't done a lot of research into what's available. I
estimated a team of ~10 people to run the event (roles listed below),
and I hoped to get local volunteers before proceeding to contact
hotels, etc. Without a strong local volunteer base, I'm not going to
try to run an event. So at this point, it seems unlikely that I'd put
in a bid for this year.

That said, some of the roles below could be filled by out of town
folks, but I'd probably lean towards helping Kevin host in Vegas if
he's considering putting in a bid.

The thing I don't like about GenCon is that, all other things being
equal (city, time of year, etc.), it's a higher cost to attend GenCon
than a pure VTES weekend.

Ira

Below are the roles that would need to be filled, though
it's possible that one person could fill multiple roles.

These are all volunteer roles. The leads would be empowered
to make decisions and run their area of responsibility, as
well as recruit additional volunteers if needed.

NAC Lead Organizer
Responsible for the overall event. Ensures all other
leads are working smoothly together.

Webmaster
Responsible for creating and maintaining the website and
e-mail lists. Maintains contact info for all the leads.
May also maintain a blog for event planning, and mid-event
updates. Tech savvy.

Hotel Liaison
Responsible for communication with the Hotel, and ensuring
everything goes smoothly with the hotel staff. Point
person on all hotel-related issues before, during, and
after the event. Preferably has experience working with
hotels.

PR Lead
Responsible for spreading word about the event far and
wide, using whatever traditional and creative means
available, including posting to message boards, getting
business cards to The Lasombra for inclusion in his sales,
etc. Outgoing and persistent, comfortable talking to lots
of people.

Hospitality Lead
Responsible for non-VTES events and hospitality for out of
town guests. Will provide information about alternate
attractions, transportation to/from the event, and
anything else to make our out of town guests feel welcome.
Enjoys helping other people have a good time.

Photography Lead
Responsible for taking pictures at the event, and
generally documenting the event. Requires good follow up
after the event to ensure pictures get posted. Must have
a camera, and a video camera might be nice, too.

Security Lead
Responsible for the security at the event. Will interface
with any police people and hotel staff on issues of event
security. Will deal with any rowdy/drunk players.
Preferably someone with security experience. May be a
moot point if we have <50 people, but with 100+ people,
this role becomes important.

Gopher Lead
Responsible for last minute requests at the event. Will
be available to get last minute items. Preferably has a
car, and will be available to run errands at any time
during the event.

Charity Lead
Optional role, but I'm hoping we'll have some charity
event or auction, so that we can donate money to a
good cause. This person would be responsible for all
aspects of our charity event.

Anything else I'm missing?

All correct. LA was distant (and therefore expensive) for a lot of
people used to going to the NAC cheaply. Attendance certainly suffered
for that. Conversely, Atlanta and all prior NAC locations were distant
and expensive for players out west.

If the only goal is attendance then we should hold the NAC in
Europe. :-)

>   I'm certainly open to suggestions as to where we think the NAC
> should be in future years.  We could keep moving from city to city.
> We could go back to GenCon.  Do we tell Seattle to just suck it up and
> deal while we try to maximize attendance, or do we try to put the NAC
> in the Pacific Northwest sometime?  Do we have it in Mexico City?

Right. You've got hard choices to make to keep it all in balance.
Maximizing attendance, so far, hasn't been the main goal, but you
certainly wouldn't want to choose a location that will struggle to
have a 15-player tournament.

>   Here's another factor: I haven't really gotten many people

> it's definitely a burden on the organizers to accomodate it - it might
> be a reason why I've gotten few volunteers.  I certainly don't expect
> to have free run of The Ram at GenCon if we were to move back.

From my perspective, the Week of Nightmares was easy to accomodate
since most venues had space available during the weekdays. It was the
weekends where they were often reluctant to have dozens of gamers
filling their biggest meeting rooms and spending zero dollars in their
catering departments.

Hey, if nobody is volunteering, see if WW would do it in Atlanta
again. If not, the default should probably be GenCon. Or to put it
another way, if there aren't any volunteers then all of the sentiment
about moving it around should be out the window and you should focus
only on maximizing attendance.

Knowing what I know now, after having done one, I'd volunteer again
but I think it shouldn't be out West for a while. Also, with the
bigger budget being offered nowadays I would have had more choices for
hotels and entertainment. It's an easier job now than it used to be.

-Robert
